messages:
maria: Heads-up: saw a regression in INT4 path for long-chat workloads after the last autotune push. 99p latency +18% on sm90 in the nightly cluster run. quick snapshot + logs: https://perf.redwood/internal/1965550123

Derek: Oof. which autotune change? the pick-score normalization or the arch overrides?

han: Looks like the new softmax-normalized pick_score made the selector oscillate for sequences >1024 tokens. kernels keep flipping between int4-opt and fp8-fallback mid-request.

maria: Exactly. The windowed selector we shipped uses a 64-token window and no hysteresis. For long sequences that see changing prefix shapes, the score delta around token 900 becomes noisy.

sasha: Can you paste the current selector config?

maria: Sure — current config in prod: 
```json
{
  "quant_selector": {
    "type": "windowed",
    "window_size": 64,
    "score_norm": "softmax",
    "hysteresis": 0.0,
    "arch_overrides": {
      "sm90": { "bias": -0.02 },
      "sm92": { "bias": -0.06 }
    }
  }
}
```

han: Two quick ideas: 1) increase window_size to 256 to stabilize transient flips, 2) add a small hysteresis (0.07-0.12) so we require sustained advantage before switching.

Derek: Also we should consider a pick_score_bias that is a function of sequence_pos. The early tokens favor int4, later tokens (long-context) should bias slightly toward fp8 for stability.

maria: I ran a microbenchmark: 100k requests varying seq 256->2048. With window=64/hysteresis=0 we see 12% tail latency regressions and 7% p50 increase. With window=256 + hysteresis=0.1 the tails drop back to baseline and int4 win-rate stabilizes at ~72%.

perf-bot: Profile uploaded: s3://ci-artifacts/1965550123/profile.tar.gz (CPU/GPU timelines + kernel-selection traces). Flame shows repeated kernel rebinds at token ~900 and extra cudaMallocs due to fallback path.

sasha: The cudaMallocs are the killer — allocator churn from switching kernels mid-request increases latency. Can we avoid switching allocations by keeping a unified workspace large enough and reusing it across paths?

han: We already have a workspace pool but fallback kernels sometimes require a different workspace alignment/size. Could add a conservative workspace size for long-seq requests when selector is unsure. 

Derek: Proposed quick fix: window_size=256, hysteresis=0.12, arch_overrides: sm90.bias=-0.08, seq_pos_bias = {">512": -0.04} (negative bias favors fp8/int-fallback less). That should reduce flip probability and allocator churn.

maria: I can push a canary change to dedicated cluster 3 with that config. Will also enable extra tracing for pick decision and workspace reuse events.

ci-bot: Canary deploy queued: canary/dedicated-3 -> config/1965550123-windowed-tweak. Run id: canary-1965550123-1

perf-bot: Running A/B against baseline: 50k requests per bucket. ETA ~ 45m. I will post perf diff when done.

sasha: Longer term: autotuner should learn a small temporal stability penalty (L2 on score deltas) so it prefers stable picks if perf delta small. Also add a per-arch "alloc_penalty" param so kernels that cause alloc churn get penalized in pick score.

han: Agreed. Add also a "kv_warmup_weight" — sequences that are cache-cold should prefer kernels that avoid expensive KV layout ops. This was biting the INT4 path for some models.

maria: Notes for the canary: enable metrics: pick_history, workspace_alloc_events, kernel_switch_count, kv_warmup_time. If switch_count > 1 per request that should be a fail signal.

Derek: If canary looks good, let's roll to host pool with gradual ramp and a rollback trigger of 3% tail-lat regression or >1.5x switch_count.

perf-bot: Canary results: window=256 + hysteresis=0.12 vs baseline => 99p latency: -6% (improvement), p50: -2%, kernel_switch_count down 88%, allocator churn down 90%.

maria: Nice. I'll open a PR with the config and a follow-up issue to add alloc_penalty and seq_pos_bias into autotuner objective.

sasha: Thanks everyone. Follow-ups: PR for config, issue for autotuner objective, add integration test that runs long-seq profile to catch oscillations. :+1:

maria: PR: https://git.redwood/repo/infra/merge/4489 - please review. I added the canary artifacts and perf graphs.

han: I'll take the autotuner objective issue. tagging: @derek for design review.

Derek: Ack. I'll review the PR today.

perf-bot: Marking thread resolved if no regressions over 24h after rollout.

maria: Closing loop: the rollout completed and metrics stayed green over 24h. Will keep the autotune redesign in backlog. Thanks all.
